title: Proper source direct image on vanishing topoi
statement: Let $S$ be Noetherian, let $X\xrightarrow{h}Y\xrightarrow{g}S$ be morphisms of finite presentation with $h$ proper, and put $f=gh$. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring killed by an integer invertible on $S$. Write $\bar h:V_f\to V_g$ for the morphism of [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles] induced by $(h,1_S)$, with constant $\Lambda$ coefficients and constructibility as in [def-trf-oriented-constructible-sheaf]. If $L\in D^b(V_f,\Lambda)$ has constructible cohomology, then every $H^q(R\bar h_*L)$ is constructible on $V_g$. If $h$ is finite, $\bar h_*$ is exact, and a sheaf $F$ on $V_f$ is constructible if and only if $\bar h_*F$ is constructible on $V_g$. In the finite case the stalk of $\bar h_*F$ at a geometric oriented point $(y,t\to g(y))$ is the finite product of the stalks of $F$ at the points $(x,t\to f(x))$ above it, with geometric $x\in X_y$.

source.place: Sections 9.1.1-9.1.2, printed pp. 19-21; finite detection follows there from the stalk formula and Lemma 8.3.3.

proof.text: The finite-presentation morphisms in the statement are finite type and qcqs. Since $S$ is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ and $Y$ Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] makes them quasi-separated. Thus their vanishing topoi admit the finite-cover triple sites of [lem-trf-qcqs-oriented-triple-presentation]. We use triples $Z=(E\to V\leftarrow W)$ with $E\to X$ and $V,W\to S$ separated etale of finite presentation, and write $H_Z=h_Z^\#$ and $G_Z=\Lambda[H_Z]$, the sheafified free constant-$\Lambda$ module on $H_Z$. This is the free sheaf characterized by maps to $F$ being sections $F(Z)$ in [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-free-separator].

source.place: Sections 8.1 and 9.1.2: the finite-cover triple site and its free sheaves.

proof.text: Choose $d$ bounding the dimensions of the fibres of $h$ by [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound], and set $c=2d$. The geometric fibres have the same dimension as the residue-field fibres by [lem-kun-dimension-extension]; they are proper by [lem-pc-proper-base-change], and finite type by the finite-presentation base-change clause of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. For every sheaf $A$ on $V_f$, [lem-trf-oriented-proper-fibre-exchange] computes $(R^j\bar h_*A)_z$ as $H^j(X_y,\phi_z^*A)$. The proper map $X_y\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ has fibre dimension at most $d$, so [lem-kun-proper-torsion-cd-bound] makes this zero for $j>c$. Its hypotheses apply to the underlying torsion abelian sheaf, and [lem-pe-left-module-derived-evaluation-forget] identifies its cohomology with the forgotten module cohomology. Finally [lem-trf-oriented-product-points-conservative] detects zero. We have proved $R^j\bar h_*A=0$ for all sheaves $A$ and $j>c$, with no constructibility assumption on $A$. This uniform bound is what will make the generator argument finite.

source.place: Lemma 9.1.1 and the finite cohomological-dimension refinement of the resolution argument in Proposition 9.1.2; Stacks 0A3V and 095U.

proof.text: Each $H_Z$ is coherent by [lem-trf-finitary-site-coherent-generators] applied to the site in Step 1. By [lem-trf-coherent-set-criterion], it is finite locally constant on a finite collection of source/base strata. On such a restriction, the free module $G_Z$ is the constant free module on that finite set, locally on the same covering. It has finite underlying set since $\Lambda$ is finite. Hence $G_Z$ is constructible by [def-trf-oriented-constructible-sheaf]. The same criterion says that the underlying set sheaf of any constructible module sheaf $F$ is coherent, in particular quasi-compact in the explicit covering-family sense of [def-trf-coherent-topos].

source.place: Section 8.1 (coherence and constructibility); Proposition 9.1.2, first paragraph.

proof.text: The representable generators give a covering family $H_Z\to|F|$, one map for each section of $F$ on $Z$. By quasi-compactness in Step 3, finitely many of these maps cover $|F|$. For each selected section the free-sheaf property [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-free-separator] gives $G_Z\to F$, sending its basis generator to that section. Their sum $P\to F$ is epic: every section of $F$ locally lies in one selected $H_Z$, and hence locally is the image of a basis generator. Local surjectivity is the epimorphism criterion [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective], and also gives an epimorphism of modules. Here $P$ is a finite sum of constructible $G_Z$, and its kernel is constructible by [lem-trf-oriented-constructible-subquotients]. Repeating with the kernel gives, for any prescribed finite $N$, exact sequences $0\to K_{i+1}\to P_i\to K_i\to0$ for $0\leq i<N$, with $K_0=F$, all $K_i$ constructible and $P_i$ finite sums of the $G_Z$. No infinite totalization or finite projective resolution is used.

source.place: Proposition 9.1.2, first paragraph: finite free generators and successive kernels.

proof.text: Fix one triple $Z=(E\to V\leftarrow W)$. Apply [lem-trf-finite-base-splits-etale] to the two separated etale maps $V\to S$, $W\to S$, obtaining a finite surjection $T\to S$ for which both are finite coproducts of opens of $T$. Pulling back triples represents inverse image by [lem-trf-qcqs-oriented-triple-presentation]. Decompose $E_T$ by the components of $V_T$; further decompose each open component of $W_T$ by its inverse images of the components of $V_T$. These are finitely many open-and-closed pieces of that component and therefore open subsets of $T$. Thus the pulled-back triple sheaf is a finite coproduct of triples $(E_a\to V_a\leftarrow W_a)$, where $V_a,W_a\subseteq T$ are opens and $W_a\subseteq V_a$, and $E_a\to X_T$ is separated etale of finite presentation. The cases of empty components give zero summands.

source.place: Proposition 9.1.2, finite-surjective base reduction, and Lemma 9.1.3.

proof.text: For each triple in Step 5 put $A_a=(u_a)_!\underline\Lambda$ on $(X_T)_{\mathrm{Et}}$, where $u_a:E_a\to X_T$, and $B_a=p_{f_T,2}^*(j_{a!}\underline\Lambda)$, where $j_a:W_a\hookrightarrow T$. The inverse-image formula in [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] identifies its representable with $p_{f_T,1}^{-1}h_{E_a}\times p_{f_T,2}^{-1}h_{W_a}$: since $V_a$ is an open containing the image of $E_a$ and $W_a\subseteq V_a$, the compatibility over $V_a$ is automatic. Taking free modules gives $G_{Z_a}\cong p_{f_T,1}^*A_a\otimes_\Lambda B_a$, by the basis bijection $\Lambda[P\times Q]\cong\Lambda[P]\otimes_\Lambda\Lambda[Q]$. This also follows from the explicit free-sheaf property [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-free-separator]. The direct-sum description of $(u_a)_!$ in [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] identifies $A_a$ with the free sheaf on $h_{E_a}$. It is constructible in the stalk-based predicate by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-free-sheaf-constructible-core], and [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison] identifies this with finite-stratification constructibility. The sheaf $j_{a!}\underline\Lambda$ is constant $\Lambda$ on $W_a$ and zero outside, so $B_a$ has the analogous two base strata.

source.place: Proposition 9.1.2, opens after Lemma 9.1.3 and the first-projection calculation.

proof.text:
Apply ordinary etale proper-image constructibility [lem-weil-pbc-etale-compactification-constructibility] to $h_T:X_T\to Y_T$ with the identity open compactification and coefficient $A_a$. It applies without a finite-dimensional hypothesis: the schemes are qcqs, $h_T$ is proper of finite presentation, and $\Lambda$ is finite. These facts persist under base change by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] and [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. The first-projection exchange of [lem-trf-oriented-proper-fibre-exchange] now gives
$$R\bar h_{T,*}p_{f_T,1}^*A_a\simeq p_{g_T,1}^*Rh_{T,*}A_a.$$
Its cohomology is constructible on $V_{g_T}$: inverse image is exact, and the constructible strata on $Y_T$ pull back along the first projection, using the single base stratum $T$ in [def-trf-oriented-constructible-sheaf].

source.place: Proposition 9.1.2, final paragraph; Stacks 0GL0, theorem-constructible-shriek, identity open compactification.

proof.text:
On $V_{g_T}$ put $B=p_{g_T,2}^*j_{a!}\underline\Lambda$, so $\bar h_T^*B=B_a$. Tensoring with $B$ or $B_a$ is exact: at each oriented point it tensors with either $0$ or $\Lambda$; inverse image commutes with tensor by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and the exact conservative points in [lem-trf-site-point-fibre, lem-trf-oriented-product-points-conservative] test exactness. The projection map
$$R\bar h_{T,*}C\otimes^L B\longrightarrow R\bar h_{T,*}(C\otimes^L\bar h_T^*B)$$
is defined by adjunction from the tensor of the counit with $1_{\bar h_T^*B}$, using the derived adjunction of [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. By the fibre formula [lem-trf-oriented-proper-fibre-exchange], at $z=(y,t)$ it is the projection map for $R\Gamma(X_y,-)$ and the constant coefficient $B_z$, which is $\Lambda$ if $t\in W_a$ and zero otherwise. In both cases this is the identity unit isomorphism or the isomorphism $0\to0$. Conservativity proves the map invertible. Take $C=p_{f_T,1}^*A_a$ and use Step 7. Exact tensor with $B$ keeps each cohomology sheaf on the base-open $W_a$ and makes it zero on the complement. Refining the base strata by $W_a$ and its closed complement proves constructibility of $R\bar h_{T,*}G_{Z_a}$ in every degree.

source.place: Proposition 9.1.2, sentence reducing the base-open generator to the first-projection generator; its stalkwise projection argument is written out.

proof.text: The finite sums in Step 5 and Step 8 show that $R\bar h_{T,*}v_f^*G_Z$ has constructible cohomology. By the base-change exchange of [lem-trf-oriented-proper-fibre-exchange] and exactness of inverse image, this is $v_g^*\mathcal H^q(R\bar h_*G_Z)$ in each degree. The map $T\to S$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. Apply [lem-trf-psi-constructibility-descent] to the sheaf $\mathcal H^q(R\bar h_*G_Z)$ on $V_g$. Its hypotheses concern $S$ Noetherian and $g$ of finite presentation, exactly our hypotheses; it does not require that this sheaf be a nearby-cycle sheaf. Thus $R^q\bar h_*G_Z$ is constructible for every $q\geq0$, and the same holds for finite sums $P$ of the generators.

source.place: Lemma 9.1.4 and Lemma 9.1.5, applied to the generator calculation.

proof.text:
Now let $F$ be any constructible sheaf. Use Step 4 with $N=c+1$. Fix $q\geq0$. Step 2 gives $R^{q+c+1}\bar h_*K_{c+1}=0$. Descend on $i=c,c-1,\ldots,0$. The long exact sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] contains
$$R^{q+i}\bar h_*P_i\longrightarrow R^{q+i}\bar h_*K_i\longrightarrow R^{q+i+1}\bar h_*K_{i+1}.$$
The first term is constructible by Step 9, and the third is constructible by the descending induction. The middle term is an extension of a quotient of the first term by a subsheaf of the third. Therefore it is constructible by [lem-trf-oriented-constructible-subquotients]. At $i=0$ this proves $R^q\bar h_*F$ constructible. Negative degrees vanish for a sheaf because direct image is right derived, and the uniform bound from Step 2 also applies. The sheaf categories have enough injectives by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], as required by the long exact sequence.

source.place: Proposition 9.1.2, free-resolution reduction, made finite using Step 2.

proof.text: For the bounded constructible complex $L$, choose a finite interval $[a,b]$ containing its cohomology. Its successive truncation triangles [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] build it in finitely many steps from $H^r(L)[-r]$, $a\leq r\leq b$. Derived direct image commutes with shifts and sends these triangles to triangles by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. Step 10 handles every $H^r(L)$. In the cohomology long exact sequence of each image triangle supplied by [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], each new cohomology sheaf is an extension of a quotient of one known constructible sheaf by a subobject of another, so [lem-trf-oriented-constructible-subquotients] applies. Induction on the finite number of truncations proves constructibility of every $H^q(R\bar h_*L)$, the first clause.

source.place: Proposition 9.1.2, passage from sheaves to bounded complexes.

proof.text:
Suppose $h$ is finite. At $z=(y,t)$ the fibre formula [lem-trf-oriented-proper-fibre-exchange] and the zero-dimensional calculation [lem-weil-pbc-zero-dimensional-cohomology] give
$$(\bar h_*F)_z\cong\prod_{x\in|X_y|}F_{(x,t)},\qquad (R^q\bar h_*F)_z=0\quad(q>0).$$
By [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], $X_y$ is the spectrum of a finite-dimensional $\Omega$-algebra: tensor the finite module generators for an affine finite model of $h$ with $\Omega$. Every prime quotient is a finite-dimensional domain over $\Omega$; multiplication by a nonzero element is injective and hence surjective, so the quotient is a field. All primes are maximal and $\dim X_y\leq0$. Properness gives separatedness, and the finite algebra generators give finite type. These verify the hypotheses of the cited calculation; nilpotents are permitted there. The product is over the finitely many geometric fibre points, not over arbitrary repeated representatives of one point. The identification of module and abelian cohomology is [lem-pe-left-module-derived-evaluation-forget]. For a short exact sequence on $V_f$, each factor stalk sequence is exact by [lem-trf-site-point-fibre], and finite products of module sequences are exact componentwise. The formula therefore makes its direct-image sequence exact at every point of $V_g$; exact conservative points detect zero kernels and cokernels by [lem-trf-oriented-product-points-conservative]. Thus $\bar h_*$ is exact and we have also proved the requested stalk formula, including the empty-fibre case (zero module).

source.place: Lemma 9.1.1 in relative dimension zero; its natural restriction maps give the finite stalk product.

proof.text: If $F$ is constructible, Step 10 gives constructibility of $\bar h_*F$. Conversely assume $\bar h_*F$ constructible. Its exact inverse image $\bar h^*\bar h_*F$ is constructible by [def-trf-oriented-constructible-sheaf]: pull a source stratum of $Y$ back by $h$, keep each base stratum of $S$, and pull back the finite locally constant module sheaves. Consider the counit $\bar h^*\bar h_*F\to F$. At $(x,t)$ its map is the projection from the finite product in Step 12 to the $x$-factor, since the fibre isomorphism is induced by restriction. This projection is surjective: extend an element in that factor by zero in the others. Exact conservative points [lem-trf-site-point-fibre, lem-trf-oriented-product-points-conservative] therefore make the counit epic. Hence $F$ is a quotient of a constructible sheaf and is constructible by [lem-trf-oriented-constructible-subquotients]. This proves detection without imposing surjectivity on $h$; an oriented point of $V_f$ already supplies its selected nonempty fibre factor.

source.place: Lemma 8.3.3 and the finite direct-image detection used at the end of Section 9.3; explicit counit argument.

Supplies the free-sheaf universal property on a small site with module coefficients, giving maps from triple generators to a sheaf. Finite covering and the kernel iteration are proved here.

Converts the source-library stalk-based predicate in the free-sheaf tool into finite-stratification constructibility for finite commutative coefficients; the unit does not replace this ordinary coefficient comparison.

Supplies commutation of derived pullback with tensor. The special base-open projection formula is proved stalkwise here using only the two values zero and Lambda.
